facts.text: Hidden Lake Colony was founded in 1996 as a daughter of Big Sky Hutterite Colony, establishing a new communal community in Glacier County.
The colony sits inside the Blackfeet Indian Reservation, drawing groundwater from the Two Medicine Formation aquifer for its farms and homes.
Hidden Lake’s residents share all agricultural labor and resources, following traditional Hutterite practices of communal living and collective crop production.
The colony operates under a 501(d) tax status, recognized by the IRS in 2009 as an apostolic religious organization.
Hidden Lake experiences a humid continental climate, with cold snowy winters, mild summers, and an average of about 12 inches of precipitation annually.
The colony’s coordinates are 48.5987° N, 112.6031° W, placing it roughly 12 miles west of Cut Bank in Glacier County.
